headline: Parliament vows tough action after attack on actress Ajmeri Haque Badhon in Italy
summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir calls the assault a 'strike against democratic governance' as the government coordinates with Italian authorities.
details: Actress Ajmeri Haque Badhon was attacked in Venice, Italy, leading to widespread condemnation and a discussion in the National Parliament of Bangladesh.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir informed Parliament on Tuesday that the attack is an assault on democratic governance and that the government will take strict action.
The Bangladesh Embassy in Rome and the Consulate in Milan are in contact with Badhon, who is expected to file formal complaints with the local police and the embassy.
The government will strongly raise the issue with the Italian Foreign Ministry to ensure justice. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has also assured Badhon of her full support.
The attackers have been identified as workers of the Awami League, a party whose activities are currently banned in Bangladesh.
Badhon has expressed her bravery in the face of the incident, stating that she will not be silenced and is determined to see the legal process through to the end.
caption:
An attack on a Bangladeshi actress in Italy sparks a national outcry and a parliamentary vow for justice.

Actress Ajmeri Haque Badhon was attacked in Venice, Italy, leading to widespread condemnation and a discussion in the National Parliament of Bangladesh.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir informed Parliament on Tuesday that the attack is an assault on democratic governance and that the government will take strict action.

The Bangladesh Embassy in Rome and the Consulate in Milan are in contact with Badhon, who is expected to file formal complaints with the local police and the embassy.

The government will strongly raise the issue with the Italian Foreign Ministry to ensure justice. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has also assured Badhon of her full support.

The attackers have been identified as workers of the Awami League, a party whose activities are currently banned in Bangladesh.

Badhon has expressed her bravery in the face of the incident, stating that she will not be silenced and is determined to see the legal process through to the end.

Source: Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Jamuna TV

headline: 9 deaths in 24 hours: Dengue toll hits highest single-day level this year
summary: 1,571 patients were hospitalised in a single day, marking a record high for 2024. The government is launching a 3-month special prevention drive.
details: At least nine dengue patients died and 1,571 others were hospitalised in 24 hours, marking the highest single-day levels for both deaths and hospitalisations this year.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), the total number of deaths has risen to 130 and total cases have reached 45,475.
The deaths were reported across several regions, including three in Dhaka South City Corporation, two each in Khulna and Dhaka divisions, and one each in Barishal and Mymensingh divisions.
Currently, 3,218 dengue patients are undergoing treatment in hospitals across the country.
In response to the surge, the Prime Minister is set to launch a three-month special campaign on Saturday to prevent the spread of the dengue virus.
The special prevention drive, scheduled to begin on September 12, is set to be a nationwide effort to combat the outbreak.
caption:
9 deaths and 1,571 hospitalisations in just 24 hours. Dengue cases in Bangladesh are hitting record highs.

At least nine dengue patients died and 1,571 others were hospitalised in 24 hours, marking the highest single-day levels for both deaths and hospitalisations this year.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), the total number of deaths has risen to 130 and total cases have reached 45,475.

The deaths were reported across several regions, including three in Dhaka South City Corporation, two each in Khulna and Dhaka divisions, and one each in Barishal and Mymensingh divisions.

Currently, 3,218 dengue patients are undergoing treatment in hospitals across the country.

In response to the surge, the Prime Minister is set to launch a three-month special campaign on Saturday to prevent the spread of the dengue virus.

The special prevention drive, scheduled to begin on September 12, is set to be a nationwide effort to combat the outbreak.
